The test image shows a soybean stem with numerous small black specks scattered across a lighter tan/gray stem, plus shriveled brown pods and some whitish material. Key candidates: Charcoal_Rot (charcoal-sprinkled microsclerotia), Diaporthe (linear pycnidia on stems), White_Mold (sclerotia + white mycelium), Anthracnose.

Let me view reference images for the top candidates.
Now let me view two more reference images to confirm before deciding.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Mature/late-season soybean stem with dense, scattered small black specks on a tan-gray stem surface; shriveled brown pods; some whitish material at lower left.
- **Septoria**: Only leaf lesions — not relevant.
- **Charcoal Rot**: "Charcoal-sprinkled" microsclerotia pattern fits the dense black speckling, but reference images show predominantly root/lower stem disease on bleached gray stems.
- **Diaporthe**: Black pycnidia on mature stems and pods — description says "small black specks form on stems, petioles, pods" at maturity, which matches well. The Diaporthe reference bottom-right panel shows a tan stem with dark pycnidia similar to the test image.
- **Anthracnose**: Black acervuli scattered on stems/pods — possible, but acervuli tend to form on lesions/cankers rather than uniformly speckling the whole stem.
- **White Mold**: Would show fluffy white mycelium prominently — not dominant here.

The dense black speckling uniformly covering a mature soybean stem with affected pods is most consistent with **Diaporthe (pod and stem blight)** — black pycnidia covering the stem and pods at plant maturity.

The distribution pattern and stage of plant maturity align with Diaporthe more than Charcoal Rot (which is more root/lower stem focused) or Anthracnose (which shows more lesion-based acervuli)."}
